name: SCRB Bihar public FIR repository (FIR search page)
publisher: State Crime Record Bureau, Bihar Police
geo_coverage: Bihar — 38 revenue districts + 12 special units (ATS, SVU, VIB, EOU, CID Patna, 4 Rail police districts)
evidence: Host unreachable (.gov.in blocked by sandbox egress proxy). Schema read from a third-party scraper fetched in full from raw.githubusercontent.com: Kantvishu/Govt-of-Bihar-Data scrape_scrb.py declares PAGES['fir']['columns'] = [sno, fir_no, fir_date, complainant, address, accused, police_station, sections, district, incident_date, status] against https://scrb.bihar.gov.in/FIRiew.aspx, with a 50-entry district-code dropdown. Same repo's README.md and CLAUDE.md report 92,424 FIR rows across 40 districts, 0 errors, scraped 2026-03-28 to 2026-03-30, and both describe the columns in prose WITHOUT 'status'. No Bihar row was seen: the repo gitignores data/.
how_to_obtain: From an Indian/unrestricted network, GET /FIRiew.aspx for __VIEWSTATE + __VIEWSTATEGENERATOR + __EVENTVALIDATION, then POST with ctl00$ContentPlaceHolder1$ddlDistrict=<code>, ddlPoliceStation='' (returns whole district), optionsRadios='radioPetioner', txtfDate/txttDate, btnSearch='Search'. Session cookie required; no login or captcha reported as of 2026-03. Alternatively ask Kantvishu for the header row plus one redacted sample row.
caveats: UNFETCHED: scrb.bihar.gov.in blocked by sandbox egress proxy on 2026-09-20; no row of this source has ever been observed by this project.
Endpoint correction: the FIR grid is FIRiew.aspx, not View_FIR.aspx which docs/INGESTION.md and BiharScrbSource.path currently target.

A 'status' column appears in the scraper's positional column list but is absent from the same repo's two prose descriptions; parse_table_rows pads short rows with empty strings so an over-declared column fails silently. Presence of any disposal/closure field is UNRESOLVED and should be assumed absent.
Row carries complainant name, address and accused name — personal data. pipeline.fir.FORBIDDEN_COLUMN matches all three. docs/INGESTION.md rule 3 applies directly.
'address' is complainant residence (victim-residence semantics), NOT offence location; it must not be used as a geography.
Declares incident_date separate from fir_date — an occurrence date Maharashtra's feed lacks. Unverified.
Third party reports the date filter on the FIR page is broken and returns all data regardless of date params, which would preclude incremental fetching.
Third party reports OutOfMemoryException on large districts (no paging control; whole district rendered at once) and frequent DNS/server outages after heavy querying.

Repository withholds sexual offences and POCSO (Supreme Court direction 7 Sep 2016) plus national-security, law-and-order and communal FIRs — a non-random censoring of exactly the categories a safety map most wants.
An FIR is a report, not a finding; withdrawn and false cases are not retracted.
District dropdown mixes 38 revenue districts with railway/special units and two police districts (Bagaha 39, Naugachhia 41) — not a clean 38-district join.
Terms of use and robots.txt unread (host unreachable); terms_reviewed must remain False.
notes: District codes read verbatim from the scraper and reproduced in the .md. Sibling pages on the same host: ArrestDetail.aspx (carries arresting-officer name and designation — 35,719 officers re-identifiable per the scraper's own analysis), deadbodies.aspx, MissingPersons.aspx (has a missing_place field finer than the station; the FIR page has no such field).

name: Maharashtra Police Citizen Portal — Published FIRs
geo_coverage: Maharashtra — all district and city police units
evidence: Harvested rows fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com and parsed. Observed 10-column grid, keys: srNo, state, district, policeStation, year, firNumber, registrationDate, firNoWithYear, sections, hasDownloadButton. Real row: {srNo 6, MAHARASHTRA, PALGHAR, BOISAR, 2025, firNumber '339', registrationDate '09/08/2025 18:07:00', firNoWithYear '0339/2025', sections 'भारतीय न्याय संहिता (बी एन एस), 2023 - 303(2) ;'}. English headers corroborated verbatim by shivam-sharma0/extract-fir-data's committed CSV header 'Sr. No.,State,District,Police Station,Year,FIR No.,Registration Date,Sections' (header-only, 78 bytes, zero data rows). Form controls agreed on by four independent scrapers.
how_to_obtain: ASP.NET WebForms POST replaying __VIEWSTATE/__EVENTVALIDATION/__PREVIOUSPAGE. Controls: ctl00$ContentPlaceHolder1$txtDateOfRegistrationFrom / txtDateOfRegistrationTo (dd/MM/yyyy), ddlDistrict (numeric, 19408 observed), ddlPoliceStation (AJAX-repopulated by ddlDistrict postback), txtFirno, btnSearch='Search', ucRecordView$ddlPageSize. Paging: __EVENTTARGET=ctl00$ContentPlaceHolder1$ucGridRecordView, __EVENTARGUMENT=Page$N. Results grid id ContentPlaceHolder1_gdvDeadBody.
caveats: NO case status, disposal or closure column — confirmed against real rows. An FIR here is a registration event with no outcome, ever.
NO crime head; category must be derived from the free-text sections string.

NO geography finer than police station. The 'coordinates' key in two harvested files was geocoded by the harvester from the police-station NAME via Nominatim/Google/MapMyIndia — every FIR at a station shares one point. It is not portal data and must not be rendered as an incident location.
registrationDate is the moment the FIR was keyed in, not when the offence occurred; no occurrence date is published.

sections fuses act and section in one cell: act name in Marathi/Devanagari, ' - ' separator, comma-separated ASCII section numbers, ';' terminator; multiple acts separated by ';' and often a literal newline.
IPC 1860 and BNS 2023 coexist in the same 2025 feed; Devanagari numerals (१९८८, २००६) appear in act names alongside ASCII years.
Selecting a district triggers a postback that WIPES both date fields; three independent scrapers re-write the dates afterwards.
The results grid element is named gdvDeadBody — stock CCTNS software copy-pasted from the dead-bodies page.
Terms of use and robots.txt unread (host unreachable from this sandbox).
notes: Contains NO personal data — pipeline.fir.audit_columns() returns [] against its column list, unlike Bihar. pipeline.fir.parse_date already handles '11/08/2025 17:52:50' -> 2025-08-11. The sibling Missing Persons grid on the same portal (table.GridTable, 8 columns: SrNo, Photo, Date of Registration, Name, Age, Incident Place, Police Station, District) does carry an Incident Place; the FIR grid does not.

name: mahagovscrapper — harvested Maharashtra published-FIR JSON dumps
geo_coverage: Nashik City and Palghar police districts, Maharashtra
evidence: Four files fetched and parsed 2026-09-20. fir-data-2025-09-27T07-41-06-426Z.json 209,602 bytes / 500 rows / only 10 unique; -with-coords.json 245,102 bytes / 500 rows / 10 unique; T08-44-14-002Z.json 9,525 bytes / 20 rows / 20 unique / 2 districts; T08-47-21-029Z.json 29,239 bytes / 60 rows / 60 unique / 2 districts, 10 distinct acts. Stations: ADAGAON POLICE STATION (Nashik City), BOISAR (Palghar). No LICENSE and no README in the repo.
caveats: The two 500-row files contain 10 unique FIRs repeated 50 times — the paging loop re-fetched page 1. Deduplicate on (district, policeStation, firNoWithYear). Anyone citing '500 Maharashtra FIRs' from this repo is citing a bug.
'coordinates' is harvester-derived geocoding of the station name, not portal data; one point per station.
hasDownloadButton is false on all 580 rows although two other scrapers click a per-row Download submit button on the live page — a parser artefact of scraping the AJAX updatePanel fragment.
Third-party harvested data, licence unstated (no LICENSE file), therefore all rights reserved by default. Held as a parser test fixture only; not for republication.
Two police stations in two districts over roughly six weeks — not representative of Maharashtra.
notes: Copied to tests/fixtures/ as cctns-published-firs-maharashtra-{20,60}rows.json and -500rows-paging-duplicates.json with provenance in tests/fixtures/README.md. Verified free of personal-data columns by pipeline.fir.audit_columns().

name: Govt-of-Bihar-Data — SCRB Bihar scraper and schema documentation
evidence: Fetched and read in full: scrape_scrb.py (331 lines), README.md, CLAUDE.md, .gitignore. Repo contains exactly 5 files (confirmed by repo-scoped code search). Declares FIR/arrest/dead/missing column lists, the SCRB ASP.NET form controls, a 50-entry district-code map, and documents four named server bugs. .gitignore excludes data/ — the claimed 92,424 FIR rows, 277,557 arrest rows and 51 dead-body rows are NOT committed.
how_to_obtain: Public repo, already read. To close the remaining schema gaps, open an issue or email the author asking only for the FIR header row and one redacted sample row — not the dataset. Zero load on the SCRB server.
caveats: This is one individual's code, not a specification. Its column names are Python variable names, not the portal's rendered headers.
Its FIR column list and its own prose disagree about whether a 'status' column exists.
Scrape is dated March 2026; server behaviour and captcha status may have changed since.
No LICENSE file; licence unstated.
notes: The single highest-value lead in this dossier: the only known party to have held a bulk Bihar FIR extract. Also documents Bihar Data Lab (statedata.bihar.gov.in, 1,109 XLSX across 40 sectors including sector 24 Police & Crime, 35 files) and Wayback-archived Bihar Police CMA monthly crime stats 2010-2021 (1,848 observations, state-level aggregates only), both separately worth cataloguing.

name: State FIR citizen-portal roster (27 states)
evidence: File fetched 2026-09-20; 27 named state citizen-portal FIR URLs extracted. Splits cleanly into an ASP.NET WebForms family (Maharashtra, Uttarakhand /Citi/firSearch.aspx, Assam /citizen/FIRDownload.aspx, Odisha /citizen/FIR_Copy.aspx, MP CitizenLogin.aspx) and a Java/JSP family behind a login (Chhattisgarh, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Jharkhand, Himachal, Arunachal, Tamil Nadu).
caveats: URLs transcribed from a third-party OSINT toolkit; NONE was opened (all .gov.in blocked). Leads, not verified endpoints.
Lists Bihar only as police.bihar.gov.in — it does not know about the SCRB FIR repository, which lives on a different host.
Roughly ten-plus states put FIR search behind a login, i.e. access:login and an RTI route, not a scrape.
No LICENSE file; licence unstated.
notes: Evidence for and against the stock-software transferability hypothesis: the CCTNS citizen portal is a programme with at least two distinct web stacks, not one binary. Confirms no ASP.NET deployment examined carries a disposal field, but does not license transferring Maharashtra's column names to Bihar — Bihar's SCRB app is a third, separate build.

name: Maharashtra Citizen Portal — Missing Persons grid (sibling page)
evidence: Row parser read from Ompawaskar/Milap backend/scrapper.js, fetched 2026-09-20: 'table.GridTable tr' with 8 columns — SrNo, Photo, Date of Registration, Name of Missing Person, Age, Incident Place, Police Station, District — plus a PersonImageHandler.ashx photo endpoint. Page itself not fetched.
caveats: Recorded only because it is the one stock CCTNS grid that carries a place of incident finer than the police station. The published-FIR grid does not.
Publishes names, ages and photographs of missing persons — out of scope for this map and must stay out; FirRecord cannot hold any of it.
Not crime-incidence data; a missing-person report is not an offence count.
'Incident Place' is free text of unknown quality and was not observed in any real row.
notes: Bihar's MissingPersons.aspx declares an equivalent missing_place field. Relevant only as evidence that the stock software CAN carry a place-of-incident and that the FIR page deliberately does not.
how_to_obtain: ASP.NET WebForms page on the same portal as PublishedFIRs.aspx; scrape the 'table.GridTable' grid, 8 columns, with per-row photos served from /Citizen/PersonImageHandler.ashx?ImID=<id>. Not recommended: the grid publishes names, ages and photographs of missing persons and nothing this project may lawfully render. Recorded for schema comparison only — see caveats.
